paragraphs: Luton Borough Council said in March 2025 that it looks after more than 300 children and young people, and that many of them live outside the town because there are not enough fostering families locally. Its children come from a wide range of cultures, faiths and backgrounds, so the council particularly wants carers from diverse ethnic backgrounds who can support a child's religion, culture and language. Singles, couples and families can all apply. The independent agencies on this page also place children from Luton.

The council pays a weekly allowance for each child, from £189 for babies to £288 for 16 and 17-year-olds, and a weekly skills fee per child that rises with experience, from £145.90 in a carer's first year with Luton to £259.13 after five years. Birthday, festive, holiday and clothing allowances are paid on top, along with a twice-yearly leave payment and a £1,000 contribution towards Council Tax. Our Luton allowance page has the full scale.

The council says the journey from first enquiry to approval usually takes around six months, and it aims to finish the assessment within 16 weeks once it starts. The steps are an information event, an expression of interest, a home visit, checks and references, a full assessment by a social worker, then fostering panel. Preparation training runs as six weekly sessions, with first aid and safeguarding included.
Speak to the council and to two or three of the agencies below to compare support and pay before you apply.
